## About Me

### Background

- I'm a clinical researcher and pharmacist by training. 
- I earned my Doctor of Pharmacy from Poona College of Pharmacy, Bharati Vidyapeeth (Deemed) University in Pune, India, where I graduated as the University Gold Medallist. 
- Before coming to Hopkins I spent two years at Indus Biotech Ltd. as an Executive in Scientific Affairs, serving as the primary sponsor contact for three concurrent randomized controlled trials and authoring protocols, Investigator Brochures, CRFs, and Clinical Study Reports end to end.

## Education

**Johns Hopkins University** | Baltimore, MD

Master of Science in Epidemiology | Aug 2025 - May 2027 

**Bharati Vidyapeeth Poona College of Pharmacy** | Pune, India

Doctor of Pharmacy | Aug 2017 - Jun 2023

## Research Interests

- My goal is to combine epidemiologic methods, biostatistical skills, and hands-on trial experience to generate trusted evidence on the safety, efficacy, and real-world viability of new medications. 
- Concretely, that means clinical trial design and conduct, systematic review and meta-analysis, pharmacoepidemiology and drug safety. 
- I'm drawn to work that blends scientific rigor, operational execution, and patient impact.

## Skills 

### Statistics & Data Analysis

- Statistical software: SPSS, STATA, R; SAS (familiar); GraphPad Prism.
- Graduate coursework: Statistical Methods in Public Health I–IV, Epidemiologic Methods I–III, Causal Inference in Medicine I, Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis, Pharmacoepidemiology.
- Primary researcher on a 212-patient prospective study of health-related quality of life in breast cancer patients (recruitment, consent, and SPSS analysis).
- Designed and piloted a survey instrument for 202 pregnant women and analyzed adherence determinants in SPSS.

### Programming

- R: comfortable with base R and basic data cleaning; new to the tidyverse and functions.
- Git and GitHub: new to version control; this site is my first GitHub repository.
- Well-versed with STATA for statistical data analysis.(140.621 to 140.624 - Statistical Methods I to IV)
- Attended SPSS course by CliMed to run different analyses on medium sized datasets. 

### Data Management & Clinical Research

- REDCap and Medidata iMedidata (EDC): CRF design, data entry, query resolution, data cleaning and digitization.
- Managed three concurrent RCTs as primary sponsor contact across 25+ site initiation, monitoring, and close-out visits under ICH-GCP E6(R2).
- Co-author on five peer-reviewed publications (see [ORCID](https://orcid.org/0009-0008-9223-845X)).
- Certifications: Good Clinical Practice (ICH-GCP), Pharmacoepidemiology and Drug Safety, Lean Six Sigma Green Belt.

## What I Hope to Learn

- Most of my analysis experience so far has been in SPSS and STATA, and I've used R mainly for coursework. 
- In Biostat 776, I want to become genuinely fluent in R as a daily tool: writing reproducible, well-organized code; using the tidyverse to wrangle real clinical and epidemiologic data; and building the version-control habits (Git and GitHub) that make collaborative research projects manageable.

## Five Fun Facts

- My PharmD gold medal was presented at convocation by the Governor of State of Maharashtra, six years of pharmacy school ending with a handshake I did not expect.
- I speak some German: I passed the Goethe-Zertifikat A2 with a 93/100, and I'd like to keep going.
- I've been invited back to my alma mater in Pune twice (2024 and 2025) as guest to conduct a lecture on careers in clinical research, in the same lecture hall I sat in as a student.
- If you take a campus tour at Bloomberg, there's a decent chance I'm leading it. I'm a Campus Ambassador and answer prospective students' questions on Unibuddy.
- My most recent research task involved digitizing handwritten vaccine cards from Mozambique, which has given me a deep appreciation for legible handwriting.

## Something Cool

I love reading books and I can finish one whole crime thriller novel in a day. Recently, I read [Sometimes I lie by Frieda McFadden](https://www.freidamcfadden.com/books/standalone-thrillers/never-lie/). The twists keep you on the edge. You can never predict what's and who's next!
